cases.severity_reason: P2: conditional pagination/protocol failure on the production artifact-read path; no universal agent hang or scientific-validity claim.

route.secondary: Artifact provenance and bounded tool output

cases.trigger: readArtifact projects a text version larger than 8 MiB; the caller follows line offsets to or past the 8389-line decodable window of a 9500-by-1000-byte fixture.
cases.consequence: The truncated flag keeps hasMore true after the readable window ends. An empty page returns nextOffset equal to the requested offset, so a caller following that protocol can repeatedly request the same unreachable page.
cases.independent_reasoning: The exact before source computes hasMore as endLine < lines.length OR truncated OR partialLine. For an empty beyond-window page pageLines is zero, endLine is offset minus one and the true truncated flag produces nextOffset equal to offset.
cases.test_reasoning: The upstream regression constructs 9,500 lines of 1,000 bytes, verifies 8,389 readable lines, requires every nextOffset to advance, requires termination and checks three beyond-window offsets return no nextOffset. Source inspection only.

cases.severity_reason: Only the named defect is absent; not whole-PR approval or runtime correctness.

cases.trigger: readArtifact projects a text version larger than 8 MiB; the caller follows line offsets to or past the 8389-line decodable window of a 9500-by-1000-byte fixture.

cases.independent_reasoning: The fixed predicate depends only on endLine < lines.length. Beyond-window offsets therefore have no nextOffset; truncated remains explicit and describeUnreachable explains the limit.

cases.severity_reason: P2: conditional audit provenance and owner-scope correctness failure. This does not establish prompt leakage, an authorization-policy bypass, or an end-to-end timeout.

route.primary: Agent orchestration / child audit authority snapshots
route.secondary: Execution provenance, notification inbox and immutable task references

cases.trigger: A native-dispatched child records an audit snapshot in a session with parent and sibling execution or task state. The before production binding gives versioningAuthorities the parent runId while requestExecutionId is the child execution ID.
cases.consequence: The child snapshot selects the parent execution provenance and includes the session-wide sibling task catalog, notification state, transfers and shell executions. Sibling changes can alter the child audit snapshot.
cases.independent_reasoning: The before caller passes runId, and the collector filters execution.turnId against that value. It also calls listSubagents and snapshot methods with sessionId only, so the output is not scoped to the child owner.
cases.test_reasoning: Corrected regression source at 070e90c asserts child provenance contains only the child execution, child.children is empty, child.task matches the child, only the child inbox and cancelled timer are captured, sibling growth leaves the child snapshot identical, and unknown/cross-session children reject. It also preserves full task history through immutable references. These source assertions were not executed.

cases.severity_reason: Only the named defect is absent; not whole-PR approval or runtime correctness.

cases.trigger: A native-dispatched child records an audit snapshot in a session with parent and sibling execution or task state. The before production binding gives versioningAuthorities the parent runId while requestExecutionId is the child execution ID.
cases.consequence: The binding supplies the child execution and task IDs, the collector selects that execution, captures only the child task reference, uses an empty child catalog and passes the child agent ID to owner-filtered snapshots.
cases.independent_reasoning: The corrected caller passes childExecution.identity.executionId and subagent.id. The collector uses executionId and subagent ID; the store rejects absent/cross-session children before serializing, and snapshot helpers constrain their SQL to session and agent.
